Subject: Throughput & burst profile validation — POC operations roster

Thanks again for the call earlier, Samir & Alex — good conversation and excited to get the POC staged. This note captures the traffic and evaluation items we agreed to as well as owners and next steps so we have a clear ops roster heading into the test.

Summary (quick):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference configuration against FastKart's real traffic patterns to hit latency and cost targets for checkout fraud scoring and product-recommendation endpoints.
- Timeline proposed: kickoff week of Dec 6, 3-week active evaluation window, final readout week of Dec 28.

Traffic intake items we need (please confirm / attach sample traffic):
1) Baseline sustained RPS and typical concurrency (avg + 95th percentile).
2) Peak RPS / burst windows (duration and frequency).
3) Average and 95th percentile token lengths for the request payloads (we're primarily concerned with input token length; embeddings/augments noted separately).
4) Typical request payload examples & a 24–48h sample CSV (timestamps, endpoint, token_count, response_size) — will help us create a realistic load generator.
5) Success criteria you want measured (latency SLOs, quality checks, and cost thresholds).

Proposed internal owners (from Redwood):
- Marissa Cole (me) — POC PM, single point of contact, overall success criteria and stakeholder updates.
- Ben Carter — infra lead (load-generation, capacity mapping, GPU config suggestions).
- Rishi Malhotra — SLO definition and quality baseline (latency/throughput guardrails).

Next steps / asks for FastKart:
- Samir: please attach the 24–48h traffic sample CSV and a short list of 3 example requests per endpoint (or a dump).
- Confirm whether you require EU data residency for logs/telemetry in the test.
- Confirm kickoff window (we're proposing Mon Dec 6 — would you prefer earlier?).

Attachments: poc-ops-roster-template.xlsx (template for owners/checklist) — I can rename if you prefer.

Thanks — once I have the sample I'll circulate a test plan and a short runbook (what we’ll hit day-by-day).

—

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the clear asks. Attached is a 48-hour extract: fastkart_traffic_sample_202611.csv (see attachment). Alex and I reviewed the list you sent and have answers inline below.

Traffic profile (FastKart production sampling):
- Baseline sustained RPS: 120 RPS (this is what our web tier sees averaged across 1h windows during peak daytime).
- Typical concurrency: 35 concurrent inference requests (95th within a 1-minute window ~ 60).
- Peak / burst: we see short spikes of 900–1,200 RPS during promotional pushes, typically lasting 30–90s, ~6–8 times per week. Longer flash sale bursts (10–12m) hit ~500 RPS and occur ~1–2x month.
- Token lengths: median input tokens ~45, mean ~62, 95th percentile ~210. Outputs vary by endpoint (recs ~30 tokens; fraud-score responses ~8 tokens).
- Payload: we attached a CSV with timestamp, endpoint, token_count, and user_id (hashed). No PII in the sample.

Success criteria (what matters to FastKart):
1) Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency < 200ms for recommendation endpoint under baseline load; p99 < 400ms for baseline. During burst windows we'd accept p95 < 450ms with graceful degradation and no timeouts for 99% of requests.
2) Accuracy/quality: recommendations precision@10 within 3% of current production baseline (we'll supply a small holdout test set).
3) Cost objective: target token-cost per 1M tokens below USD 18 during steady-state (we want Redwood recommendations on quantization/config that balance cost & quality).
4) Reliability: no more than 0.1% 5xx error rate across the duration.

Other notes / asks:
- We need to ensure telemetry (logs/traces) for the POC are retained in us-east for now. EU residency not required for this proof.
- Alex will coordinate with your infra team on sampling instrumentation — Alex.reed@fastkart.com.

Attached: fastkart_traffic_sample_202611.csv (48h sample), poc-success-metrics-draft.xlsx (initial list of KPIs).

If this looks right I can confirm kickoff the week of Dec 6 — prefer Tue Dec 7 for a 30-minute runbook walk.

—

Redwood POC roster / owners

- SLOs & quality monitoring: Rishi Malhotra — will own p95/p99 measurement and the precision@10 checks against your holdout set.

3) Legal/Proc: if you want to fast-track a limited-scope POC agreement, I'll introduce our contracts lead — otherwise the POC can proceed on the standard eval terms.

I'll send the calendar invite for Tue Dec 7 10:00am ET and a short Google Drive folder with the runbook and synthetic traffic generator artifacts.

Appreciate the speed here — we'll aim to have a first probe (baseline) run within 48hrs of kickoff.
